exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Trust Dependencies
exploitedBy.relevance: Directly relates to implicit trust relationships between network segments that attackers can exploit to move laterally.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Boundary Bridging
exploitedBy.relevance: Covers techniques for bridging network boundaries by exploiting implicit trust between segments.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
exploitedBy.relevance: Insufficient egress filtering enables attackers to exfiltrate data using alternative protocols that bypass controls.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exfiltration Over Unencrypted Non-C2 Protocol
exploitedBy.relevance: Lack of egress filtering allows unencrypted exfiltration over non-standard protocols to go undetected.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Disable or Modify Network Device Firewall
exploitedBy.relevance: Overpermissive ingress ACLs represent a misconfiguration of network device firewall rules that attackers can exploit.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Indicator Blocking
exploitedBy.relevance: Attackers exploit monitoring blind spots to block or avoid generating indicators at the network boundary.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Sniffing
exploitedBy.relevance: Blind spots in boundary monitoring can enable undetected network sniffing at segment boundaries.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Valid Accounts
exploitedBy.relevance: Shared credentials across zones allow attackers to use valid accounts to authenticate and move between segments.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Credential Stuffing
exploitedBy.relevance: Shared credentials increase the risk of credential stuffing attacks succeeding across multiple zones.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Adversary-in-the-Middle
exploitedBy.relevance: Attackers can intercept management plane communications to propagate trust and manipulate traffic between zones.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Protocol Tunneling
exploitedBy.relevance: Routing protocol leakage can be used to create tunnels that bypass boundary controls between network segments.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Address Translation Traversal
exploitedBy.relevance: NAT traversal techniques can complement VLAN hopping to cross segment boundaries undetected.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: External Remote Services
exploitedBy.relevance: Split tunnel VPNs are a form of external remote service that can be exploited to bypass segment boundaries.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Disable or Modify System Firewall
exploitedBy.relevance: Firewall rule shadowing involves manipulating firewall rules so that overly permissive rules override restrictive ones.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Disable or Modify Cloud Firewall
exploitedBy.relevance: Rule shadowing in cloud environments involves modifying cloud firewall policies to create unintended permissive paths.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Non-Application Layer Protocol
exploitedBy.relevance: Using non-application layer protocols for tunneling between zones can evade application-layer inspection controls.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Domain or Tenant Policy Modification
exploitedBy.relevance: Stale boundary policies can result from unauthorized or untracked policy modifications that degrade zone separation over time.
